classification.difficultyReason: Combine shifts, reflection and scaling, then solve shifted-square equations for intercepts and position them consistently around the vertex in each sketch.

content.prompt: Sketch the graph of each of the parabolas below. Label the turning point and any axial intercepts.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=x^2$ two units right and one unit up. The turning point is $(2,1)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=2$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=(0-2)^2+1\\y&=5\end{align*}$$
For an $x$-intercept:
$$\begin{align*}0&=(x-2)^2+1\\(x-2)^2&=-1\end{align*}$$
There are no real $x$-intercepts. Sketch an upward-opening parabola through $(0,5)$ with minimum $(2,1)$.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=x^2$ one unit left and two units up. The turning point is $(-1,2)$ and the axis is $x=-1$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=(0+1)^2+2\\y&=3\end{align*}$$
For an $x$-intercept:
$$\begin{align*}0&=(x+1)^2+2\\(x+1)^2&=-2\end{align*}$$
There are no real $x$-intercepts. Sketch an upward-opening parabola through $(0,3)$ with minimum $(-1,2)$.

spec.description: Upward-opening parabola with labelled minimum and y-intercept.

answer.worked:
Reflect $y=x^2$ in the $x$-axis, then translate one unit right and three units down. The turning point is $(1,-3)$ and the axis is $x=1$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-(0-1)^2-3\\y&=-4\end{align*}$$
For an $x$-intercept:
$$\begin{align*}0&=-(x-1)^2-3\\(x-1)^2&=-3\end{align*}$$
There are no real $x$-intercepts. Sketch a downward-opening parabola through $(0,-4)$ with maximum $(1,-3)$.

answer.worked:
Reflect $y=x^2$ in the $x$-axis, then translate two units left and one unit down. The turning point is $(-2,-1)$ and the axis is $x=-2$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-(0+2)^2-1\\y&=-5\end{align*}$$
For an $x$-intercept:
$$\begin{align*}0&=-(x+2)^2-1\\(x+2)^2&=-1\end{align*}$$
There are no real $x$-intercepts. Sketch a downward-opening parabola through $(0,-5)$ with maximum $(-2,-1)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5(d); teacher PDF page 3, printed page 332
spec.description: Downward-opening parabola entirely below the x-axis.
spec.mathematics: y=-(x+2)^2-1; vertex (-2,-1); y-intercept (0,-5); no real roots.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=x^2$ two units right and one unit down. The turning point is $(2,-1)$ and the axis is $x=2$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=(0-2)^2-1\\y&=3\end{align*}$$
At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}0&=(x-2)^2-1\\(x-2)^2&=1\\x-2&=\pm1\\x&=1\text{ or }3\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening parabola through $(0,3)$, $(1,0)$ and $(3,0)$ with minimum $(2,-1)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5(e); teacher PDF page 3, printed page 332
spec.description: Upward-opening parabola with all intercepts and minimum labelled.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=x^2$ three units right and four units down. The turning point is $(3,-4)$ and the axis is $x=3$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=(0-3)^2-4\\y&=5\end{align*}$$
At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}0&=(x-3)^2-4\\(x-3)^2&=4\\x-3&=\pm2\\x&=1\text{ or }5\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening parabola through $(0,5)$, $(1,0)$ and $(5,0)$ with minimum $(3,-4)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5(f); teacher PDF page 3, printed page 332
spec.description: Upward-opening parabola with all intercepts and minimum labelled.

answer.worked:
Reflect $y=x^2$ in the $x$-axis, then translate two units right and one unit up. The turning point is $(2,1)$ and the axis is $x=2$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-(0-2)^2+1\\y&=-3\end{align*}$$
At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}0&=-(x-2)^2+1\\(x-2)^2&=1\\x-2&=\pm1\\x&=1\text{ or }3\end{align*}$$
Sketch a downward-opening parabola through $(0,-3)$, $(1,0)$ and $(3,0)$ with maximum $(2,1)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5(g); teacher PDF page 3, printed page 332
spec.description: Downward-opening parabola with all intercepts and maximum labelled.

answer.worked:
Reflect $y=x^2$ in the $x$-axis, then translate two units left and four units up. The turning point is $(-2,4)$ and the axis is $x=-2$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-(0+2)^2+4\\y&=0\end{align*}$$
At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}0&=-(x+2)^2+4\\(x+2)^2&=4\\x+2&=\pm2\\x&=-4\text{ or }0\end{align*}$$
Sketch a downward-opening parabola through $(-4,0)$ and $(0,0)$ with maximum $(-2,4)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5(h); teacher PDF page 3, printed page 332
spec.description: Downward-opening parabola; origin labelled as a required intercept, without an O label.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=x^2$ one unit right and two units down. The turning point is $(1,-2)$ and the axis is $x=1$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=(0-1)^2-2\\y&=-1\end{align*}$$
At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}0&=(x-1)^2-2\\(x-1)^2&=2\\x-1&=\pm\sqrt2\\x&=1\pm\sqrt2\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening parabola through the three intercepts with minimum $(1,-2)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5(i); teacher PDF page 3, printed page 332
spec.description: Upward-opening parabola with exact surd intercept labels.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=x^2$ two units left and three units down. The turning point is $(-2,-3)$ and the axis is $x=-2$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=(0+2)^2-3\\y&=1\end{align*}$$
At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}0&=(x+2)^2-3\\(x+2)^2&=3\\x+2&=\pm\sqrt3\\x&=-2\pm\sqrt3\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening parabola through the three intercepts with minimum $(-2,-3)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5(j); teacher PDF page 3, printed page 332
spec.description: Upward-opening parabola with exact surd intercept labels.

answer.worked:
Reflect $y=x^2$ in the $x$-axis, then translate two units right and two units up. The turning point is $(2,2)$ and the axis is $x=2$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-(0-2)^2+2\\y&=-2\end{align*}$$
At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}0&=-(x-2)^2+2\\(x-2)^2&=2\\x-2&=\pm\sqrt2\\x&=2\pm\sqrt2\end{align*}$$
Sketch a downward-opening parabola through the three intercepts with maximum $(2,2)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5(k); teacher PDF page 3, printed page 332
spec.description: Downward-opening parabola with exact surd intercept labels.

answer.worked:
Reflect $y=x^2$ in the $x$-axis, then translate two units left and three units up. The turning point is $(-2,3)$ and the axis is $x=-2$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-(0+2)^2+3\\y&=-1\end{align*}$$
At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}0&=-(x+2)^2+3\\(x+2)^2&=3\\x+2&=\pm\sqrt3\\x&=-2\pm\sqrt3\end{align*}$$
Sketch a downward-opening parabola through the three intercepts with maximum $(-2,3)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5(l); teacher PDF page 3, printed page 332
spec.description: Downward-opening parabola with exact surd intercept labels.

answer.worked:
Dilate $y=x^2$ vertically by a factor of $\frac12$, then translate one unit right and two units down. The turning point is $(1,-2)$ and the axis is $x=1$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=\frac12(0-1)^2-2\\y&=-\frac32\end{align*}$$
At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}0&=\frac12(x-1)^2-2\\\frac12(x-1)^2&=2\\(x-1)^2&=4\\x-1&=\pm2\\x&=-1\text{ or }3\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening parabola, wider than $y=x^2$, through the three intercepts with minimum $(1,-2)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5(m); teacher PDF page 3, printed page 332
spec.description: Vertically compressed upward-opening parabola with exact intercept labels.

answer.worked:
Dilate $y=x^2$ vertically by a factor of $\frac12$, then translate two units left and one unit down. The turning point is $(-2,-1)$ and the axis is $x=-2$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=\frac12(0+2)^2-1\\y&=1\end{align*}$$
At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}0&=\frac12(x+2)^2-1\\\frac12(x+2)^2&=1\\(x+2)^2&=2\\x+2&=\pm\sqrt2\\x&=-2\pm\sqrt2\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening parabola, wider than $y=x^2$, through the three intercepts with minimum $(-2,-1)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5(n); teacher PDF page 3, printed page 332
spec.description: Vertically compressed upward-opening parabola with exact surd intercept labels.

answer.worked:
Dilate $y=x^2$ vertically by a factor of $\frac13$ and reflect in the $x$-axis, then translate two units right and three units up. The turning point is $(2,3)$ and the axis is $x=2$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-\frac13(0-2)^2+3\\y&=\frac53\end{align*}$$
At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}0&=-\frac13(x-2)^2+3\\\frac13(x-2)^2&=3\\(x-2)^2&=9\\x-2&=\pm3\\x&=-1\text{ or }5\end{align*}$$
Sketch a downward-opening parabola, wider than $y=-x^2$, through the three intercepts with maximum $(2,3)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5(o); teacher PDF page 3, printed page 332
spec.description: Vertically compressed downward-opening parabola with all intercepts labelled.

answer.worked:
Dilate $y=x^2$ vertically by a factor of $2$ and reflect in the $x$-axis, then translate one unit left and two units up. The turning point is $(-1,2)$ and the axis is $x=-1$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-2(0+1)^2+2\\y&=0\end{align*}$$
At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}0&=-2(x+1)^2+2\\2(x+1)^2&=2\\(x+1)^2&=1\\x+1&=\pm1\\x&=-2\text{ or }0\end{align*}$$
Sketch a downward-opening parabola, narrower than $y=-x^2$, through $(-2,0)$ and $(0,0)$ with maximum $(-1,2)$.
